question: What causes the filed WebKit "Target page, context or browser has been closed" / page-crash flakes (d1-migration, d2-duty-items, d3 startup recovery)?

observations.result: WebKit pages crashed or closed across seven unrelated specs (crew-management-gate "Page crashed", d1, d2, d3-startup-recovery, u08-duties); Chromium projects showed only one timing bound miss.

observations.run: d1-migration + d2-duty-items, WebKit, 3 repeats, retries 0, one worker, idle machine
d1-migration + d3-startup-recovery, WebKit, one worker, process sampling every 0.8 s
observations.result: One WebKitWebProcess peaked at 2,087 MB; free memory fell to 736 MB of 8,035 MB; 15 of 15 passed

observations.run: App alone in WebKit (production build), empty course and one course
observations.result: ~665-685 MB on both H1 (a25eba1) and now: engine/WASM baseline of Playwright WebKit on Windows, not a regression

classification: Environmental memory pressure: tests that hold legacy, current and reopened database instances in one WebKit page reach ~2 GB; with a second browser competing on this 8 GB machine the WebKit content process is killed. Single-worker idle runs are clean. Not reproduced as an app defect.
consequence: The local browser suite stays on one worker (OWNER_DECISIONS.md entry 3). CI retains traces even when a retry turns the run green, so a recurrence on CI can be read rather than guessed.
notDone: Lowering per-test peak memory (closing each database instance before opening the next inside the harnesses) would make WebKit tolerate parallel runs; left as a T1 follow-up if the owner wants workers on a bigger machine.
